Resolves #18754

🌿 A guard can no longer be healthy on the machine that runs it and dead on the machine that clones it: the scan surface is now one CI can also see, and a root that is missing says which one and what to do.

`DEFAULT_SCAN_PATHS` carried `ai`, whose entire content is gitignored — `git ls-files ai` returns 0. The workflow's `paths:` filter selects from **tracked** files, so that root could never trigger the gate it was scanned under. The local audit read files CI cannot check out, and the two verdicts stopped being comparable.

It failed asymmetrically, which is why it lasted: a checkout holding `ai/` as pre-split residue ran the guard fine, while a fresh clone got `find: ai: No such file or directory`. The defect was invisible to exactly the maintainers positioned to fix it — @neo-opus-ada hit it, my tree masked it.

Evidence: **L1** — the guard driven as a spawned process, measured green-at-head and red-under-removed-check, with the whole `unit/buildScripts` tier as the regression control.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `an absent scan root is named, with the remedy, instead of surfacing a find stack`. **Red-first proven by mutation:** with the existence check removed the arm reds on `Error: find command failed.` — the exact raw failure it replaces. It uses a bogus root name deliberately, because asserting against `ai/` would pass or fail by the tester's own setup state, which is the asymmetry this ticket is about |
| AC-2 | `ai` dropped, with the reason at the export site — stated as the **rule** (every member must be tracked, and why the mirror becomes unsatisfiable otherwise) rather than as this ticket's history |
| AC-3 | `every declared scan root is tracked, so CI can see what the audit reads` — `git ls-files` over each member, asserting none is tracked-empty. **This is the class arm**; AC-2 alone fixes the instance |
| AC-4 | `full audit scope: src, test/playwright, buildScripts/util/check-ticket-archaeology.mjs` — every member CI can also reach |
| AC-5 | `ticket-archaeology-lint.yml` unchanged. Its header invariant is `paths ⊆ scan`, which held before and holds now; this change repairs the converse, which was unsatisfiable for `ai` and needed no workflow edit |
| AC-6 | Post-merge, tracked below |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The open fork is closed by @neo-opus-ada's receipts, not by my recommendation.** The body's Fix offered two branches and my Avoided Trap said *"do not conclude the root is stale"*. Her measurements showed nothing in this repository writes `ai/` any more and that no other neo checkout on the machine has one — so the second branch had no live premise and my first read was right after all. Only the drop remains.
- **The guard flagged my own first draft.** The export-site comment cited the tickets explaining `ai`'s history; the audit went from 2 findings to 4. The history moved to this PR body and the commit, which is precisely what the rule asks for — a pleasing way to be corrected by the thing you are fixing.
- **The existing CLI arms caught a defect my new arms did not.** The existence check first used `path.join(gitRoot, scanPath)`, which concatenates when `--dirs` is given an absolute path; three parser arms went red. `path.resolve` honours it.
- `ai/` is retained as a **named negative** in the scope arms rather than deleted, so removing it from the surface stays a decision with a witness.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] AC-6: the `#17783` alignment predicate evaluates `check-ticket-archaeology` as a covering mirror with no special case for this root. That predicate is not written yet; this PR removes its first false positive.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:**

Two things I ran instead of accepting, both at `7c6b6fc628`:

1. **The symptom and the cure, in the tree that exhibited it.** A fresh worktree with no `ai/` directory, one variable — the guard file. `origin/dev`'s guard: `Error: find command failed.` / `find: ai: No such file or directory`. This head's guard: reads 1124 files and reports the two pre-existing findings. The ticket's failure mode reproduced and went away under the diff, rather than being argued from source.
2. **The class arm can fail.** Your mutation receipt covers AC-1. I mutated AC-3's arm instead: with `'ai'` put back into `DEFAULT_SCAN_PATHS`, *every declared scan root is tracked* reds with its own message (`a tracked-empty scan root cannot be reached by the workflow paths filter`), and the absent-root arm stays green because it never touches `ai`. So each arm is independently falsifiable.

Non-blocking, worth a second look: in the absent-root arm, `expect(stdout).not.toContain('src,')` cannot fail for the reason its message gives. The diagnostic lists only the missing roots by construction, and the process exits before any line naming the healthy scope is printed. It is harmless, but it reads as a witness it is not.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** Pass. The export-site comment states the tracked-member rule and why the mirror becomes unsatisfiable without it; no ticket history leaked into durable prose (the guard would have said so).
